newsitem.title: FRANCE: Macedonia poll said marred by registration snarls.
newsitem.headline: Macedonia poll said marred by registration snarls.

text.p: Macedonian local elections were "essentially fair and orderly" but were marred by widespread registration problems, a delegation of monitors from the Council of Europe concluded on Wednesday.
The monitors from the council's Congress of Local and Regional Authorities of Europe said they found registration snarls "in almost all of the polling stations visited" during Sunday's poll.
"Such problems may have affected the results of the elections in some local authorities," the council said in a statement.
Many citizens were unable to vote because their names did not appear on the electoral list, the monitors said, adding that the problem was most common in northwestern Macedonia.
Unofficial results indicated that there would have to be runoff elections on December to decide the make-up of most of the 124 councils at stake.
The results took no account of opposition appeals expected over allegations of fraud and widespread reports of irregularities on the electoral lists.

The delegation's conclusions were at odds with an earlier report by an observer mission from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, which gave the elections a clean bill of health after saying it saw no proof of any problems that would cast doubt on the result.
The Council of Europe was created after World War Two to foster democracy and human rights across Europe.
